name: LM358DR
title: LM358, LM2904, LM258, LM158 families: dual general-purpose op amps, 3 V to 36 V
summary: Dual bipolar op amps for single or split supplies whose input range reaches the negative rail. The B versions (LM358B, LM358BA, LM2904B, LM2904BA) run from 3 V to 36 V at 300 µA per channel with 1.2 MHz bandwidth and EMI filtering; the original LM358, LM2904, LM258 and LM158 types run from 3 V to 30 V (26 V for LM2904) at 350 µA per channel with 0.7 MHz bandwidth. LM358DR is the LM358 in an 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel, rated 0 °C to 70 °C.

circuits.title: Inverting amplifier, gain -3.6
circuits.description: One amplifier of the pair inverts and scales the input: VIN reaches the inverting input through RI, RF returns the output to the same node, and the non-inverting input sits at ground. With RI = 10 kΩ and RF = 36 kΩ the gain is -3.6, so a ±0.5 V input gives about ±1.8 V out. The part runs from ±12 V. The second amplifier is not used.
notes: The input signal source returns to GND.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier with supply bypass
circuits.description: Amplifier 1 as a non-inverting stage: VIN reaches IN1+ through RIN, RG ties IN1- to ground and RF returns OUT1 to IN1-, so the gain is set by RF and RG. A low-ESR ceramic capacitor bypasses V+ to ground at the pin; a second one bypasses V- and is fitted only when V- is a negative supply (with one supply, V- is ground). The second amplifier is not used.

operation.text: Twelve dual op amps share this document. LM358B, LM358BA, LM2904B and LM2904BA are the newer B versions of LM358 and LM2904: 3 V to 36 V supply, 300 µA per channel typical, 1.2 MHz unity-gain bandwidth, unity-gain stable, internal RF/EMI input filtering, 2 kV HBM ESD, and offset no more than 3 mV (2 mV for the BA parts) at 25 °C. LM358, LM358A, LM2904, LM2904V, LM258, LM258A, LM158 and LM158A are the original types at 0.7 MHz and 350 µA per channel. The grades differ in supply range, offset and bias limits and temperature range (family comparison table). LM358DR is the LM358 in SOIC-8 on tape and reel, rated 0 °C to 70 °C.

Each package holds two independent op amps with high gain and internal frequency compensation, made to run from a single supply across a wide voltage range. Split supplies also work when their total lies inside the recommended supply range and the positive supply stays at least 1.5 V above the input common-mode voltage. The supply current hardly changes with supply voltage, and the parts run directly from a 5 V logic supply.
The B versions have a 1.2 MHz unity-gain bandwidth and a 0.5 V/µs slew rate.

The valid input range runs from ground (V-) to VS - 1.5 V, narrowing to VS - 2 V over temperature. An input may rise above VS, up to the maximum supply rating, without damage. The output has the right polarity as long as one input stays inside the valid range; with both inputs outside it the output polarity is undefined. If an input goes more than 0.3 V below V-, its current must be held to 1 mA and the output polarity is undefined.
The amplifiers are on whenever supply is applied; there is no enable or shutdown. They run from a single supply or from dual supplies.
Signals may be applied to the inputs before VS is present, which suits systems with several supplies.
One amplifier's output may be shorted to ground indefinitely at TA of 25 °C or below with VS at 15 V or less. A short from an output to a supply rail can overheat the part and eventually destroy it.
Supply voltage above the recommended range can damage the part permanently. A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor close to each supply pin keeps noise from a noisy or high-impedance supply out of the amplifier.

Put a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor from each supply pin to ground as close to the package as possible; on a single supply one capacitor from V+ to ground is enough. Keep analog and digital grounds apart and watch where ground current flows; a ground plane on an inner layer spreads heat and lowers EMI pickup. Route input traces away from supply and output traces, and if one must cross a noisy trace, cross at right angles. Mount RF and RG right next to the inverting input so its parasitic capacitance stays small, keep input traces short, and a guard ring driven from a low-impedance node around sensitive traces cuts leakage from neighbouring traces at other potentials.

In the non-inverting layout, RG and RF sit right at IN1- and RIN at IN1+, the input traces run away from the supply lines, the V+ bypass capacitor sits at the V+ pin, a V- bypass capacitor is added only for dual-supply use, and the ground plane is on another layer.

The supply must span more than both the input and the output signal ranges: scaling ±0.5 V to ±1.8 V works from ±12 V. Resistor values in the kilohm range suit the milliampere-level currents of the circuit and keep the part from drawing too much current.
Parts compliant to MIL-PRF-38535 have every parameter tested unless noted; on other parts not every parameter is necessarily tested in production.
Automotive (AEC-Q100) versions LM2904-Q1, LM2904B-Q1 and LM2904BA-Q1, and Enhanced Product versions LM258A-EP and LM2904-EP, exist as separate parts.
